title: Independence of Cartan--Eilenberg comparison maps on the derived spectral sequence
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ be Grothendieck abelian categories [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian], let $F:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ and $G:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ be additive left exact functors [def-sp-left-exact-additive], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism in $\mathcal A$. Choose injective resolutions $X\to J_X^\bullet$ and $Y\to J_Y^\bullet$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions] and Cartan--Eilenberg injective resolutions of $F(J_X^\bullet)$ and $F(J_Y^\bullet)$ as supplied by [lem-sp-cartan-eilenberg-exists]. Any two choices of comparison maps lifting $f$ give the same maps, from the second page onward, between the spectral sequences of the filtration by the Cartan--Eilenberg resolution degree on the total complexes after applying $G$ [def-sp-double-complex-total]. These maps compose as the maps induced by $f$ compose, and the isomorphisms of the second pages with $R^pG(R^qF(-))$ and of the abutments with $H^{p+q}(\operatorname{Tot}G(I))$ commute with them.

proof.text: Use the supplied presentations, rather than choose new resolutions. Apply the bounded-below second-filtration construction with bound zero to their mapped bicomplexes. A degreewise map preserving the finite supremum of diagonal images lifts through each filtration step, giving the filtered comparison maps. Identity and composite comparisons are explicit structures.

Apply Mathlib InjectiveResolution.descHomotopy to the two injective-resolution lifts of the same original morphism. Extend the homotopy by zero and apply F. Subtract the two CE comparisons and apply the double-complex null-homotopy theorem directly. Homotopy.equivSubZero restores the comparison homotopy. An additive functor preserves the finite diagonal coproducts because all but finitely many summands vanish. The second-filtration steps are split summand subobjects, so their splittings transport through G. The map/extend natural isomorphism then transports the filtered homotopy to the mapped presentations.

Apply filtered homotopy invariance to the resulting one-step-lowering homotopy to obtain equality of the entire spectral-sequence maps. Compare arbitrary identity and composite lifts with the explicit identity and composite comparisons; use the functor laws of M.S.

Apply the natural two-column image computation to the bicomplex obtained by applying G before extension. Compose its image isomorphism with M.pageIso. M.naturality and cancellation of the target image inclusion prove the page-two naturality square. Evaluate horizontal cohomology termwise: injective cycles and boundaries give the normalized left-exact cohomology comparison. Preserve kernels to identify its cycle map as an isomorphism; the normalization and epi cancellation make the comparisons natural, and componentwise naturality assembles them into isomorphisms of the vertical complexes. The horizontal augmentation determines an explicit injective resolution of H^q(F(J)); Mathlib isoRightDerivedObj and its naturality identify the iterated cohomology with R^pG(R^qF(X)).

Take the abutment objects to be total cohomology and use the image filtration. The degreewise stable quotient theorem gives finite image filtrations and stable cycle-boundary quotient pages. Compare these quotients with M.pageIso using the quotient-image comparison and uniqueness of the transition map. Homotopic maps have equal cohomology maps. The induced image maps preserve the image filtration; functoriality gives identity and composition.
